These JSON files are frozen test oracles. Rust tests consume the data directly; no Python interpreter is needed to run them.

The Windows document-catalog capture used UTC+09. Its original
`datetime.fromtimestamp` contract uses the runner's local timezone. The native
fixture test independently verifies the stored calendar dates against UTC+09,
then binds only `modified` and undated `date`/`recent` fields to the same input
mtime in the runner's timezone. It never derives expectations from native
output; the frozen JSON, epoch mtimes, dated filename dates and all other fields
remain unchanged.

`documents-python-baseline.json` records retained distinct pure helper calls from theme commit `8c5b71d2f1074bb5d1d831fa395617bf4ae2abc8`. The original document, routing, pin, tab, renderer, base-install, updater and workspace-mod suites ran 113 tests on Windows: 98 passed and 15 were explicitly skipped because their fixtures require symlink privileges, executable POSIX scripts, macOS launchd, or an enabled live WebKit renderer. Filesystem-dependent `seed_config` captures were replaced by native sandbox tests. User home paths were replaced by synthetic fixture paths and the unchanged Python functions recomputed their expected outputs. Path-dependent Windows captures execute on Windows; portable captures execute on every platform. Native tab creation substitutes the new executable path for the two original Python entry-point paths when comparing the unchanged tab structure.

`pinned-agent-plan-baseline.json` records 168 retained calls from the Apache-2.0 Workspace Mods release `9aa50108fc3cc3c3af0fb376f0bb1760c90af3a6`. Its original collector, metadata, Node-discovery, plan-usage and reset suites ran 81 tests on Windows: 69 passed and 12 were explicitly skipped for POSIX executable fixtures, POSIX named-session fallback, or SQLite fixture handles surviving Windows temporary-directory cleanup. Aggregate tuple keys are serialized as `provider:session`; captured fallback dates prevent a later test run changing the weekly window. Metadata log fixtures use repeated-record encoding to preserve the original bounded-tail behavior without storing large padding files. These tests never contact providers or consume real reset credits.

The native installation sandbox tests additionally exercise preserved personal settings, complete-mod replacement, candidate validation, error-free verification, focus preservation, portable configuration seeding, rejected paths, and rollback after an unhealthy candidate. They use an isolated fake app CLI. These checks do not establish live desktop, audio, launchd, WebKit, credential-store, or provider-server acceptance; those require separate platform evidence.

`renderers_macos.rs` runs the two original live HTML renderer cases by default on macOS (short-page margins and viewport/late-content height). Its additional combined WebKit/Mermaid integration is an explicit opt-in test through the native wrappers. It compiles both renderers into a temporary app home, uses a public Mermaid library, and checks real PNG sizes, content settling, width buckets, invalidation and cache reuse. It never connects to an app/core or installs into the user's home. CI must set `HERDR_RENDER_LIVE=1` and `HERDR_TEST_MERMAID_JS`, then run the ignored renderer test explicitly; an optional `HERDR_RENDER_EVIDENCE` path receives a sanitized success receipt only after every assertion passes. Merely compiling or ignoring this test is not platform acceptance evidence.

`documents-workspace-cli.json` captures five original `set_workspace_icon` CLI executions and four unchanged `seed_workspace_pins.seed` calls from the same theme baseline. Icon cases preserve existing Unicode settings, exact JSON separators/no final LF, empty-background omission, tint, unsupported-extension status, and copied modification time. Seed cases record exact subprocess arguments and final selection for creation success, creation failure, empty original selection and local casefold matching. The native integration tests run a guarded fixture executable; an explicitly ignored comparison also runs the original archived CLIs against that executable when an external Python/archive is provided. The five added document corpus records cover absent spaces and untouched preview leaves without creating null fields. These cases use only synthetic settings and disposable files.

`workspace-focus-upstream.json` is separate from the original 97-file migration baseline. It records exact upstream commit `fb3c2343843254ae7aee81fb6de3b014b7597d60`, source SHA-256 values, 71 unchanged helper calls and restoration-boundary captures for all ten original fake-window scenarios in the newly added `tests/test_workspace_focus.py`. That unchanged original suite passed all ten tests during capture. Native pure tests consume the frozen outputs; a separate refusing-app subprocess target checks finally integration and offers an opt-in exact-upstream original CLI comparison. The known failed/ID-less-creation versus concurrent newly selected terminal ambiguity is preserved, not resolved. These records do not replace live desktop acceptance.

`media-image-baseline.json` captures ten valid image fixtures against the unchanged embedded `PYTHON_IMAGE` fallback, plus ten unchanged `json.dumps` serialization examples (including DEL, non-ASCII and scientific float notation). PNG, baseline/progressive JPEG and VP8/VP8L/VP8X WebP bytes were generated once with Pillow 11.2.1; native tests consume their base64 bytes without Pillow/Python. SVG cases include BOM, Unicode/DEL filenames, scientific viewBox dimensions and a root after a leading comment longer than 1 MiB. The latter intentionally retains the original Linux/Windows 300x150 bounded-read fallback; macOS uses its separate full-file Foundation path. Native CLI tests check source-spelling-sensitive nanosecond signatures, numeric types, cache hashes/full bytes/reuse/invalidation. An ignored external-original comparison checks JSON stdout serialization and cached bytes directly against the archived embedded script. These checks do not claim macOS AppKit/PDFKit execution.


Dedicated lifecycle policy fixtures moved to their external provider with the implementation. They are not part of this release or its test counts.

The usage corpus excludes one provider-owned parked-session result, preserved with that adapter. The document kinds fixture uses the neutral `localViews` option in place of an irrelevant former provider option; its general-kind expectations are unchanged.

CLI help fixtures describe optional local tools and exclude the removed service-update option. Other retained parser outcomes remain exact.
